sentences.text:
Applicant :- Mithai Lal
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. And 3 Others
Counsel for Applicant :- Pradeep Kumar Yadav

Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Manoj Bajaj,J.
Applicant has approached this Court through this application under Section 482 Code of Criminal
Procedure for issuance of directions to the Additional District Judge court no.13, Allahabad to
expedite and conclude the proceedings of Sessions Trial No.1091 of 2022, titled State versus Sunita
@ Anita, arising out of case crime no.0195 of 2022, under Sections 498A, 304B I.P.C. and 3/4 D.P.
Act, Police Station Mauaima, District Prayagraj, in a specific time period.

Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the case crime no.0195 of 2022, under Sections 498A, 304B I.P.C. and 3/4 D.P. Act was registered at Police Station- Mauaima, District Prayagraj on the basis of the complaint by the applicant- victim and trial in the said case commenced against accused after framing of charges on 10.05.2023.
He further submits that out of total 19 prosecution witnesses only one witness i.e. P.W.1- Mithai Lal has been examined by the trial court so far.
He submits that it would be in the interest of justice, if, trial in the above case is expedited.
He prays that necessary directions be issued to the trial court for expediting the trial.

sentences.text: After hearing the learned counsel and considering his submissions, this Court finds that after registration of the first information report, the final report under Section 173(2) Cr.P.C. was filed on 12.11.2022 and thereafter, the charges against the accused persons were framed by the trial court on 10.05.2023.
Since, the trial against the accused commenced only few months back, therefore, it is not a case of inordinate delay in conclusion of trial.

Recently, the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Shaikh Uzma Feroz Hussain Vs. The State of Maharashtra, vide order dated 10.11.2023 passed in Writ Petition(s) (Criminal) No. 587 of 2023, has observed that the Constitutional courts should be slow in fixing a specific time frame for conclusion of trial pending before the court of original jurisdiction.

entities.text: Shaikh Uzma Feroz Hussain Vs. The State of Maharashtra
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Resultantly, this Court is not inclined to exercise the inherent powers under Section 482 Code of Criminal Procedure, as no exceptional ground is made out for issuing the directions as prayed for.
The application fails and is dismissed.
